paragraphs: It was five o'clock on Wednesday, January twentieth, and Lily came home from school. She opened the door and stopped. Pip did not run to meet her, and the hall was empty. Small wet footprints crossed the floor from the bathroom door across the hall. Lily put down her bag of school stuff and looked at the footprints. "Whose footprints are these?" she asked. Tom stood behind her with his arms crossed and a puzzled look on his face. "Footprints do not appear by themselves," he said, "so this is a good mystery."

Tom knelt on the floor and looked at the footprints. "They are not mine, because they are too small," he said. "They are not Dad's, because his feet are much bigger." He pointed at one print with his pencil. "Look, there are four toes." Lily held up four fingers and smiled. Mom stood at the kitchen door with the phone in her hand. "I washed Pip at four o'clock," she said. "Then I answered the phone, and I talked for a long time." "Pip hates baths, and he smells awful," said Lily. "I guess that he ran away from his bath."

The children searched the hall for more clues. The prints were fainter and fainter, and they disappeared at the door of Tom's room. Tom pushed the half-open door slowly. Pip sat on Tom's striped towel, and the red ball lay between his paws. His fur was clean, wet, and fluffy. Lily and Tom laughed. Pip looked at them with big eyes.

"Whose towel is this?" asked Lily. "It is mine," said Tom, "and now it is wet." "It has blue and white stripes, and it is my favorite." Pip wagged his tail and dropped the ball. "Whose ball is that?" asked Tom. "It is Pip's red ball," said Lily. "He took it to the softest place in the house." It was not a surprising end, because Lily guessed the answer in the hall.

Mom came to the door and saw the wet puppy. "I am sorry, Pip," she said. "Next time, I will shut the bathroom door." Tom lifted Pip. Lily picked up the wet towel. There was water everywhere, so the children tidied up the floor. "Now I know Pip's secret," said Lily. "He hides in the softest place when he does not want a bath." Pip sneezed, and everybody laughed again.
